summary: Iter 44 - Riwayat Pembayaran (payment history for piutang & hutang). Backend 5/5 pytest passed: GET /api/piutang default returns only belum/sebagian (lunas sales excluded); GET /api/piutang?all=true additionally includes lunas sales that have payments[], each row carries sisa; GET /api/hutang mirrors the same semantics for purchases; lunas sale without any payments entry is NOT included even with all=true (verified by seeding a cash-complete sale and asserting absence); payment dates (via /transactions/{id}/pay and /purchases/{id}/pay) persisted correctly (date[:10] matches input). Frontend: Hutang & Piutang page (/hutang-piutang) renders expandable history toggle hp-history-toggle-{id} with payment count. Expanded PaymentHistory table renders first-row 'Bayar awal (saat transaksi)' / 'Bayar awal (saat pembelian)' (date = sale/PO created_at) when initial amount_paid > sum(payments), followed by 'Cicilan ke-N' rows with Tanggal Bayar, Dicatat oleh, Jumlah and running 'Sisa Setelah Bayar'. Checkbox hp-show-lunas reloads with ?all=true: lunas sale/purchase appears with hp-lunas-{id} badge and no Bayar button. Bayar modal on Hutang tab: hp-pay-amount + hp-pay-date -> hp-pay-submit; after submit new 'Cicilan ke-1' row appears in history with the selected date (20 Jan 2026) and 'Admin' as recorder.
critical_code_review_comments: list_piutang/list_hutang (server.py L1063, L1159): using {'$or': [q, {'payments.0': {'$exists': True}}]} is correct; however the inner q uses $in which is fine. Note that a sale that was fully paid at creation (amount_paid = total, payments=[]) is intentionally excluded from all=true since there is nothing to show. Behavior matches spec.

PaymentHistory.jsx 'initial' uses doc.amount_paid - sum(payments). When a sale was fully paid upfront (payments=[]) and show-lunas is checked, this never surfaces because the backend filter payments.0 excludes it (good). But a mixed case 'initial=0 and payments non-empty' renders only cicilan rows (correct).

server.py pay_transaction/pay_purchase still store payments[].date as f'{date[:10]}T{now_iso()[11:]}'. Consistent, but a dedicated 'date' (YYYY-MM-DD) vs 'at' (full timestamp) separation would improve clarity (previously noted).
Frontend load() fires two parallel GETs on every showAll toggle - fine today, but a shared loader guard would avoid race in slow networks.
